payload.source_label: The q-Riemann symbol denotes the similarity-solution value along x/t = 0 for data q_l and q_r

contract.statement: For the hyperbolic equation under study, take the Riemann problem with constant left state q_l on x < 0 and constant right state q_r on x > 0 initially. The q-Riemann symbol applied to these data denotes the state in its similarity solution along x/t = 0. This state is often used to define numerical fluxes [raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2.1 and equation (1.11); raw PDF page 33, printed page 11, Section 1.7 final paragraph]. The passage introduces notation and does not specify general existence or uniqueness conditions or a point-value convention at a stationary discontinuity [same defining paragraph].
assumptions: The relevant problem is a Riemann problem for the hyperbolic equation under study, with q_l on x < 0 and q_r on x > 0 initially [raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2.1 and equation (1.11)].

The defining paragraph presupposes a similarity solution supplying a value along x/t = 0; it does not state a separate existence, uniqueness, or admissibility theorem [raw PDF page 33, printed page 11, final paragraph, anchor “the value that arises in the similarity solution”].

The notation refers to the one-dimensional Riemann problem introduced in Section 1.2.1, explicitly cross-referenced by the defining paragraph [raw PDF page 33, printed page 11, final paragraph; raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, equation (1.11)].

Both scalar and system settings occur in the source; the definition does not restrict the output to a scalar [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, scalar case m = 1; raw PDF page 33, printed page 11, m-vector convention].

The surrounding Riemann discussion includes linear and nonlinear equations, so a particular constant-coefficient advection formula is not part of this general notation definition [raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, final sentence; raw PDF page 28, printed page 6, continuation of Section 1.2.1].
quantifiers: q_l and q_r denote the specified constant left and right initial states of a Riemann problem; their roles are fixed by x < 0 and x > 0 in equation (1.11) [raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2.1].

x and t denote spatial position and time; the defining evaluation uses the similarity coordinate x/t [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, introduction to equation (1.1); raw PDF page 33, printed page 11, final paragraph].

The hyperbolic equation under study and its state space are contextual parameters, not displayed arguments of the q-Riemann symbol [raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7 opening paragraph; raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, definition of a Riemann problem].
